answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public, slashable bond before it may submit work or claim rewards. If several identities collude to fake independent demand, auditors can compare their repeated payment paths and shared counterparties; proven coordination forfeits the bonds. The velvet interface may tell a fable of effortless participation, but reaching the summit of influence then requires real capital per identity, and a successful attack risks losing it.
